Argondal had walked over 2000km. A few weeks ago they had left the outpost and the central roost still wasn't in sight. His heavy cart loaded with his anvil and weapons was pulled by his trustworthy Landwalker. Woof was clearly tired. They would have to camp for the night.

Slowly they descended down the spiral road from the treetop walkways to the forest floors. There was a secured town here with a tavern. At the tavern he enjoyed a Zillfruit while the Landwalker enjoyed a bucket of Gnaw. "Yes and they arrange your belongings at night! I'm telling you!" A schryke male was enthusiastically telling to a Med'ja He had heard the superstitions before, he might have noticed it himself. But he was sceptical there really was a thing like that.

Argondal wasn't the best Holnareem smith, at the southern roost there was so much competition it was hard for him to stand out. Hopefully the competition was less at the great roost, and if not he would go further, there had to be a place were his Holnareem craftsmanship would stand out.

As he left the bar intoxicated he noticed a Firow teasing around his head trying to lure him. Paying it no head he made a bed next to his cart and fell asleep.

--------

At the great roost competition was almost as fierce as in the southern roost. Many Holnareem were selling swords of better making, foreign Deva made weapons were available here and the seafairers ships seemed to flow in without end.

Argondal sat at his stand, petting Woof, dangling a Gnaw for him to eat. Woof jumped to grab it and landed in a shock on the wooden floor boards of the central market. A patrol approached and schrieked at him to not do that. He fed a tail wagging Woof another gnaw in a more orderly fashion and the patrol trudged off.

This would be his second week without a sale, his funds were getting low. Like this he wouldn't even have enough left to make the trip back.

It was at this faithful day he once more drank a Zillfruit and encountered a Firow trying to lure him. He had been hesitant to follow the Firow in the woods they were as likely to guide you as they were to trick you. Argondal had nothing to lose, he followed the Firow down to the forest floor and until they reached a cavern opening. Then the Firow fled.

He entered.

A fire was burning, a smelting furnace, his anvil, his chair and some of his weapons were in this cavern! He rubbed his face, that Zillfruit must have been over date.

Then he saw something that made him doubt his alcohol use even more. His swords were smelting themselves. A bunch of detailing tools, that Argondal never used for holnareem don't have fine motor skills, was used to [Detail](http://www.ashokaarts.com/img/product_images/image/detail/antique-turkish-or-balkan-qama-dagger-wwwashokaartscom-fine-antique-oriental-arms-and-armour-swords-and-weapons-8-2324.jpg) the swords and sheets. Fascinated he stared at the impossible display of his swords adorning themselves then he dreamed off.

He awoke in a daze. "What a strong Zillfruit!" He opened his eyes and saw that he hadn't made it up. He was in a cave, 15 of swords and 5 daggers had been adorned with intricately embellished in a way no Holnareem could. *Woof*

He grabbed the swords and moved through the crevice out of the cave. Woof was wagging his tail before the entrance. "Woried huh? Don't be, this will be a wonderful day."

At his stand he displayed the best sword with pride. His first sword was bought quickly. Soon more and more buyers took notice and because he was a kind Holnareem he got pushed over on the price, selling it for not even a third of what a regular sword would cost. Before noon he was sold out. He hadn't made much, but he was so happy he had sold so many swords, he had even sold 60 regular swords along with the intricate ones.

Tonight he would go back to that cave with less scepticism. Maybe the spirits of order were real.
